source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Council Bluffs OCB1 carries 9 MW of IT capacity, which at AI training density is roughly 225 racks and under 100 accelerators, making it a regional colocation asset rather than a hyperscale AI node.

Disclosed capacity is the exception in Iowa. The state has 52 mapped data center sites, and only two publish power figures, totaling 18 MW. OCB1 accounts for 9 MW of that, half the declared total. Any estimate of Iowa data center load therefore rests on a small disclosed fraction, and the true figure is higher.

The certifications describe the workload the campus was built for, not the workload it runs. PCI DSS, HIPAA, FISMA, HITRUST and TIA-942 point to regulated enterprise and federal tenants, which typically run below AI training density. The 420,000 square feet of technical space fits a multi-hall regional campus rather than a single large AI cluster. At 40 kW per rack, 9 MW supports roughly 225 racks.

Power procurement, interconnection status, on-site generation and expansion plans are absent. The suitability score of 56 is computed from published IT capacity and operator type alone, and it lists announced expansion as missing. Coordinates are unset, so the facility cannot be placed against transmission infrastructure. The data establishes the size of one campus, not whether it constrains AI scaling in Iowa.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
